Norton Church Of England Primary School
Come and Visit Our School – Reception 2027
We are very excited to be welcoming new families to our school as you begin your journey towards starting Reception in September 2027.
Rather than holding traditional open days, we are delighted to welcome families for individual 1:1 visits. This gives you the opportunity to experience our school in a more personal way, see our wonderful learning environment, and get a real feel for school life.
During your visit, you will have the chance to tour the school with our Headteacher, who will be happy to answer any questions you may have and talk to you about what makes our school such a special place for children to learn and grow.
We would love to meet you and show you around!
To arrange a visit at a time that is convenient for you, please contact our school office on 01452 730531.
We look forward to welcoming you and your family to our school.
_______________________________________________________________________________________
Our Vision is for all of our children to shine like stars:
(our vision celebrates fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect and tolerance for different faiths and beliefs)
Our school has 4 houses:
Strive
that our children lead happy and fulfilled lives through seeing the best in others and in themselves; they are resilient, forward looking and appreciative
Think
that our children have the essential knowledge, skills and behaviours to guarantee that they thrive in modern Britain; the wisdom to preserve the beauty of our planet; the wisdom to make informed, positive decisions
Act
that our children celebrate differences and value everyone in our Norton family and wider community; they celebrate belonging to a local, national and international community and they expect inclusion
Respect
our children know that everyone has the right to be themselves. Norton is a place where everyone can feel safe, be happy and learn. Everyone at our school is equal and acts with respect and kindness towards each other. Our children respect themselves and are proud to be part of an inclusive school.
We welcome children each morning from 8.40am. All children are expected to be in school by 8.55am, ready for registration. At the end of the day, children can be collected between 3.15-3.30pm.
Our school is at the heart of the community:
Norton Church Of England Primary School is situated in the heart of Norton Village, has many unique qualities and strengths. With 155 pupils on roll there is a wonderful community spirit. We are big enough to offer a good range of activities and facilities, yet small enough to offer a personal touch - every child matters. Children can start at our pre-school from 3 years old.
Norton Little Learners is situated within the school building. This makes for a smooth transition into the school as the children are familiar with the school environment early on. Children leave at the age of 11 when they go on to a variety of local secondary schools.
Mrs Farren (Head Teacher) likes to meet each family individually and show them round the school to see it in action and answer any questions. Most Friday afternoons we have a sharing assembly which a lot of our parents attend. Prospective parents have the opportunity to join us for this assembly.Please contact Mrs Higgins or Mrs Farren on 01452 730531 to arrange a convenient date and time.

Vision and Goals
Our Pre-school Vision
‘Those who are wise will shine like the sky and those who lead others to goodness will shine like the stars forever’ Daniel 12:3
At Little Learners, we believe that every child is a shining light, unique and valued. Our motto, “We all shine like stars,” reflects our commitment to nurturing wisdom, kindness, and faith in all we do.
Linked to the school houses—Strive, Think, Act and Respect (STARS)—we encourage our Little Learners to shine: work hard, be thoughtful, make positive choices, show respect, and let their light shine brightly. Rooted in Christian values, we aim to inspire every child to grow in confidence, character, and love, making a difference in our Pre-school, community, and beyond.
Early Years Foundation Stage Framework
Activities are planned based on the development matters statements of the EYFS Framework. The areas of learning are:
· Personal Social and Emotional development: Children’s personal, social and emotional development (PSED) is crucial for children to lead healthy and happy lives, and is fundamental to their cognitive development. Underpinning their personal development are the important attachments that shape their social world. Strong, warm and supportive relationships with adults enable children to learn how to understand their own feelings and those of others.
· Communication and Language: The development of children’s spoken language underpins all seven areas of learning and development. Children’s back-and-forth interactions from an early age form the foundations for language and cognitive development. The number and quality of the conversations they have with adults and peers throughout the day in a language-rich environment is crucial. By commenting on what children are interested in or doing, and echoing back what they say with new vocabulary added, practitioners will build children’s language effectively.
· Physical Development: Physical activity is vital in children’s all-round development, enabling them to pursue happy, healthy and active lives. Gross and fine motor experiences develop incrementally throughout early childhood, starting with sensory explorations and the development of a child’s strength, co-ordination and positional awareness.
· Mathematics: Developing a strong grounding in number is essential so that all children develop the necessary building blocks to excel mathematically. Children should be able to count confidently, develop a deep understanding of the numbers to 10, the relationships between them and the patterns within those numbers.
· Literacy: It is crucial for children to develop a life-long love of reading. Reading consists of two dimensions: language comprehension and word reading. Language comprehension (necessary for both reading and writing) starts from birth. It only develops when adults talk with children about the world around them and the books (stories and non-fiction) they read with them, and enjoy rhymes, poems and songs together. Skilled word reading, taught later, involves both the speedy working out of the pronunciation of unfamiliar printed words (decoding) and the speedy recognition of familiar printed words. Writing involves transcription (spelling and handwriting) and composition (articulating ideas and structuring them in speech, before writing).
· Expressive art and design: The development of children’s artistic and cultural awareness supports their imagination and creativity. It is important that children have regular opportunities to engage with the arts, enabling them to explore and play with a wide range of media and materials. The quality and variety of what children see, hear and participate in is crucial for developing their understanding, self-expression, vocabulary and ability to communicate through the arts. The frequency, repetition and depth of their experiences are fundamental to their progress in interpreting and appreciating what they hear, respond to and observe.
· Understanding the world: Understanding the world involves guiding children to make sense of their physical world and their community. The frequency and range of children’s personal experiences increases their knowledge and sense of the world around them – from visiting parks, libraries and museums to meeting important members of society such as police officers, nurses and firefighters. In addition, listening to a broad selection of stories, non-fiction, rhymes and poems will foster their understanding of our culturally, socially, technologically and ecologically diverse world. As well as building important knowledge, this extends their familiarity with words that support understanding across domains. Enriching and widening children’s vocabulary will support later reading comprehension
Characteristics of effective learning
In planning and guiding what children learn, we continually reflect on the different rates at which children are developing and adjust our practice appropriately. We ensure that our planned activities provide opportunities for the three characteristics of effective teaching and learning to be present. These are:
· Playing and exploring: finding out and exploring, playing with what they know, being willing to ‘have a go’.
· Active learning – motivation: being involved and concentrating, keep trying and enjoying achieving what they set out to do.
· Creating and thinking critically – thinking: having their own ideas, making links and choosing ways to do things.

Reflections
Year 6 reflections on school life
The photos below capture Year 6 students (Leavers 2024) reflections on their time at school, contemplating how our school vision and Christian values have shaped their journey.
They were asked to think about how our vision, inspired by Daniel 12:3—“Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens”—has helped them grow and flourish throughout their years. The students shared how embracing our Christian values of courage, friendship, peace, forgiveness, truthfulness, and thanks has influenced their personal development, friendships, and approach to challenges.
These reflections showcase how the foundation of our faith and values has supported their growth, both academically and spiritually, preparing them to shine brightly as they move forward onto their next stages of life.

School Worship
Worship during the week at Norton:
Each class has a list of prayers and each day a child rolls the dice to decide which prayer they do before going out to lunch. The children take the lead for this in every class, where needed staff will always support with reading.
The school prayer is said at the end of every day either in class or at collective worships.
Our school prayer is based on our school houses and encourages us to think about how we act ourselves and as part of our school community:
Support us to be positive as we stretch out and STRIVE hard to reach our goals, and live out our Christian values,
Teach us to THINK about how we treat others and to use kind words and actions,
Always guide us to ACT responsibly when we want something to change in our school,
Remind us to RESPECT and celebrate everyone in our school community,
SHINE your love on us our Lord
Daily worship structure:
Christian vision worship
Key stages Christian value worship
Infant class and Junior class
Christian value worship
Individual classrooms
Every class in their own classroom

Whole school and parents/carers
Children involvement:
Children are the central part of every worship at Norton, and are always eager to be involved and help in any way they can. Their confidence in delivering worship and their enthusiasm to help shows how much they take our Christian values on board.
These are just some of the things they may do during a worship:
- Collect the objects needed for worship (Bible, Cross, Candle)
- Light and blow out the candle
- Write and say the prayer
- Read/act out a story
- Lead the dancing during singing worship (Dance club have started to create dances to some of the worship songs)
- Collect a worship helper sticker for helping!
Worship evaluations:
We always welcome feedback from anyone who attends one of our worships in school, why not use the form below to evaluate a worship you’ve attended and hand it in to the school office. Thank you.

Values
At our school, our Christian values guide everything we do, shaping our daily lives and school worship. We encourage friendship, fostering kindness and support for one another. Forgiveness teaches us to show grace and understanding. With courage, we face challenges with strength and faith. Thankfulness reminds us to appreciate the blessings around us. We strive for peace, creating a caring and respectful community. Through truthfulness, we uphold honesty and integrity. These values help us grow as individuals, reflect God’s love, and build a nurturing school family.
At our school, our Christian values shape not only our daily lives and worship but also how we serve our wider community:
With courage, we stand up for what is right and help those in need. We try new things and always have a go.
Friendship encourages kindness and inclusion, both in school and beyond.
We promote peace by fostering harmony in our school, the local community and the wider community.
Forgiveness teaches us to show grace and understanding to others.
Thankfulness reminds us to appreciate and share our blessings.
Through truthfulness, we build trust and integrity in all we do.
These values inspire us to make a positive difference in our own lives, our school life and also in the world around us.

Our Pebble Bowl
At Norton, we have a special pebble bowl where each pebble represents every member of our school community—both children and staff. Just as every star in the sky shines uniquely, each pebble is different, symbolizing our individuality while reminding us that we all belong and matter equally.
When someone becomes part of our Norton school community they place a pebble in the bowl. When the time comes for them to sadly leave our Norton family they take a pebble with them so they know they will always be a part of our family and community.

Christian Distinctiveness
How do we embrace and live out the Church of England’s vision for education?
Norton C of E Primary school is shaped by the Church of England’s Vision for Education, which emphasizes the development of the whole child—academically, socially, and spiritually. We provide a nurturing environment where children are encouraged to grow in character, develop a love for learning, and contribute positively to the world around them. Through a broad and engaging curriculum, strong pastoral care, and a commitment to serving our community, we ensure that every child is valued and supported. This vision underpins all that we do, helping our pupils to flourish and truly shine like stars in all aspects of their lives.
At Norton, our Christian distinctiveness is at the heart of all we do, guiding and inspiring our community. Rooted in our vision from Daniel 12:3, “Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens,” we believe every child has the potential to shine like stars!
Our Christian values—courage, friendship, peace, forgiveness, truthfulness, and thanks—shape our daily interactions, fostering a nurturing and inclusive environment where children grow academically, socially, and spiritually. These values underpin all that we do at Norton; individually, as a school community, a local community and a wider community.
Our school motto, “We all shine like stars,” reflects our commitment to helping each child flourish with wisdom, kindness, and integrity. Through our STARS framework — Strive, Think, Act, Respect—we encourage pupils to develop their character and leadership within our school houses. Together, we create a school where faith, learning, and love shine brightly in all we do.
How do we celebrate this at Norton?
Every Friday, our school community gathers for our Sharing Assembly, a special time of celebration that reflects our Christian distinctiveness.
Rooted in our vision from Daniel 12:3, “Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens,” we recognise and encourage the ways our children shine in their learning, character, and faith.
Each class awards a Star of the Week to a child who has demonstrated perseverance, kindness, or excellence, reflecting our belief that we all shine like stars. We also present a Christian Value Award to a child who has lived out one of our core values—courage, friendship, peace, forgiveness, truthfulness, or thanks—in their daily actions.
With parents joining us in this uplifting celebration, our Sharing Assembly reinforces the Christian values at the heart of our school, inspiring every child to grow, flourish, and shine.
SIAMS inspection
We are delighted that our most recent SIAMS inspection recognised the strength of our Christian vision and the positive impact it has across every aspect of school life. Inspectors found that our vision is clearly understood and lived out by pupils, staff and leaders, shaping decisions, nurturing strong relationships and enabling everyone to flourish. The report celebrated our inclusive and caring community, where every individual is valued and supported, as well as the meaningful role of collective worship in inspiring reflection, joy and shared values. It also recognised the quality of our Religious Education curriculum, which develops pupils’ understanding of Christianity alongside a range of worldviews and faiths. We are proud that the inspection affirmed our commitment to providing a nurturing, inclusive and aspirational environment where all can grow, belong and thrive.

Church links
Church links in school:
We value the important role our local church plays in the life of our school and are looking forward to developing and revitalising these links as we await the appointment of a new vicar. Interviews are taking place imminently, and we are hopeful that this will mark the beginning of an exciting new chapter in our relationship with the local benefice.
In the meantime, we are incredibly grateful to our supporting vicar, Reverend Phillipa, who has kindly stepped up to support the benefice during this interim period. We are particularly thankful for her support in helping us to welcome iSingPOP into school this October. The children came together to learn songs and perform a special concert for their families and the wider community, celebrating wonderful Christian values through music and singing. It was a special celebration of our school and wider community, bringing people together from across the locality to share in the joy of singing, friendship and faith.
We look forward to building on opportunities like this and welcoming a new vicar into our school community to worship with us, celebrate our Christian faith and help strengthen our links with the local church.
Church links in school in photographs:
Below are some photos showing one of the prayer spaces our previous vicar came in to do with the junior children. They were reflecting on themselves, the wider community and the world. With a theme of peace running throughout. After explaining each station, the children were left to self-guide themselves to each one.
One prayer left by the children read:
“Dear Lord, Help everyone who needs it most because I’ve got what I need. Amen”
Our previous vicar AKA Chris Tingle, came in to run a christingle worship teaching us all about the traditional link to candlemass. We then enjoyed creating our own christingles in our classes.
Our local churches:
We love visiting our local churches as part of our school community, creating special moments of worship and reflection. While we have a strong connection to Norton Church, we have sadly outgrown the space for larger gatherings. When possible, we visit Sandhurst Church for special services, such as our Christmas celebrations, where we can come together as a whole school. These visits allow our children to experience the beauty of worship in a church setting, deepening their understanding of faith and strengthening our bond with the wider Christian community.

Welcome to Norton Primary
A welcome from Mrs Farren
I am proud to lead a wonderful team who are dedicated, skilled and caring. Everyone who works at Norton has shared values and aims; ensuring that each child reaches their full potential. We know that this can only be achieved when children feel confident enough to learn from their mistakes and challenged to reach personal goals in a happy and exciting learning environment.
The school continues to go from strength to strength. We have grown from teaching in mixed age classes to single year groups which is hugely beneficial when looking at the progression of the curriculum. We are big enough to provide an array of clubs and extra- curricular activities; small enough to know each child and family individually.
We have had much to celebrate over the past few years….
We were one of the first schools in Gloucestershire to achieve Mental Health Champion status and have highly trained staff members who guide children through life’s challenges with great skill and care.
Our Sporting achievements include winning both boys and girls football tournaments and leagues. We have a talented sports coach who ensures quality P.E teaching across all year groups, focussing on fundamental skills and building every child into the best sports person they can be.
We have high academic expectations and teaching is consistently strong from Reception to Year 6 with teachers leading groups in the County for Maths.
Norton team provides exciting learning opportunities where children can express themselves and develop their self-confidence. With a strong moral base running alongside excellent teaching, we support children to become successful, confident individuals ready for the challenges of secondary school and beyond.

that our children have the essential knowledge, skills and behaviours to guarantee that they thrive in modern Britain; the wisdom to preserve the beauty of our planet; the wisdom to make informed, positive decisions
Our School

Visits and Visitors
Diwali dance and diya painting
In November, over two days, our school hosted vibrant Diwali-themed workshops where every student had the chance to celebrate the Festival of Lights through creative and engaging activities. The Diya Painting workshop allowed children to design and paint their own Diya oil lamps, learning about Diwali’s symbolism of light triumphing over darkness while exploring Indian culture. In the Indian Dance workshop, students enjoyed a dynamic experience, learning a range of dance styles from graceful Kathak, with its intricate hand gestures and storytelling, to the energetic Bollywood fusion that blends traditional Indian moves with modern Western choreography. These interactive workshops fostered creativity, teamwork, and cultural understanding, making Diwali a memorable and educational celebration for the entire school.
Coming up this term…
Year 4 and Year 5 have got an exciting joint trip to Tewkesbury, they will be visiting the John Moore museum for half the day and Tewkesbury Abbey for the other half…
They will be looking for signs of salvation around the Abbey to link to their current topics in RE and also interviewing staff at the Abbey - this will also link to other subjects as all information they gather on this trip will be used to create leaflets. There may be some creative art opportunities arise throughout the day as well… we can’t wait!

Art, Design and Technology
At Norton C of E Primary School, Art, Design and Technology links closely with our school vision.
Children strive to develop their creativity, imagination and practical skills, think creatively and critically as designers, artists and problem-solvers, developing the knowledge and skills needed to thrive in modern Britain, act by expressing their ideas, exploring possibilities and celebrating the creativity and achievements of others, and respect different cultures, artistic traditions, ideas and perspectives, understanding that everyone is equal and has the right to express themselves.
Art, Design and Technology teaching at Norton inspires children to be creative, curious and confident in expressing their ideas. We encourage children to explore a wide range of artists, designers, craftspeople, materials and techniques, whilst developing an understanding of how creativity and design have shaped the world around us. Through drawing, painting, sculpture, textiles, construction, mechanisms, cooking and designing and making, children develop their ability to experiment, take risks, solve problems and communicate their ideas.
Children develop a greater understanding and knowledge of art, design and technology, as well as their place within the wider creative world. They are encouraged to appreciate the work of others, celebrate differences and understand how art, design and technology are influenced by different cultures, societies and periods of history. The Art, Design and Technology curriculum at Norton allows children to develop knowledge and skills that can be used across other curriculum areas, whilst also supporting their spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
Our curriculum is designed to develop children’s knowledge, skills and creativity progressively throughout their years at Norton and into their further education. Children are encouraged to become independent and resourceful thinkers who can design, create, evaluate and improve their work, whilst developing a lifelong appreciation of creativity, craftsmanship and innovation.
We are fully inclusive and appropriate adaptations are made for children with additional needs so that they can access and participate in the Art, Design and Technology curriculum. Every child is given the opportunity to be creative, develop their skills and experience success, regardless of their starting point or level of ability.Art intent
By the time our children have finished their time at Norton we know that they will be:
Confident in their abilities as an artist.
Knowledgeable about a range of artists and famous artwork, reflecting on the impact these have had.
Have the capabilities to use a range of art skills such as sketching, painting, sculpting, collaging and printing.
Find similarities and links between their own artwork and artist’s artwork.

Modern Foreign Languages
French Intent
Key principles that underpin our French Curriculum:
At Norton we believe that learning a foreign language allows children to develop an understanding of different cultures. It can be the key to opening up interest and confidence in communicating with people from all around the world.
We want children at Norton School to see that foreign language learning is developing the art of communication; understanding that even if they do not know everything they can see or hear, they are still able to respond and communicate.
Norton’s vision for the acquisition of a foreign language is that pupils:
Understand the value of learning an additional language
Understand how cultures differ but can all co-exist harmoniously
Develop confidence in an additional language and respond to written and spoken language
Recall grammatical structures in different tenses and make links to the English equivalents
Firstly speak, then write at increasing length in an additional language
Through the high quality first teaching of French taking place we will see the impact in the following ways:
Children will be able to communicate with each other in French.
Children will become aware that a language has a structure, and that the structure differs from one language to another.
Children will develop their language through development of the four key skills of speaking, listening, reading and writing.
Children will enrich their language learning by developing an understanding of the French culture.
Children will learn how language skills can be applied to a range of languages.
Children will transfer to KS3 effectively and successfully and will be well prepared to continue and develop their language skills.
Lead staff member: Miss Eaton

Music
At Norton C of E Primary School, music links closely with our school vision.
Children strive to develop their musical skills and confidence, think creatively and critically as musicians, act by expressing themselves through music and celebrating the musical achievements and traditions of others, and respect different cultures, musical styles and traditions, understanding that everyone has the right to express themselves.
Music teaching at Norton inspires children to develop a love and appreciation of music that will stay with them for the rest of their lives. We encourage children to be curious about music and to explore a wide range of musical styles, genres, cultures and traditions. Through listening, singing, composing, performing and learning musical instruments, children develop their creativity, confidence and understanding of the world around them.
Children develop a greater understanding and knowledge of music, as well as their place within the wider musical and cultural world. They are given opportunities to perform, share and celebrate music together, developing their ability to collaborate, communicate and express themselves.
Our curriculum is designed to develop children’s musical knowledge and skills progressively throughout their years at Norton and into their further education. Children are encouraged to become confident musicians who can appreciate, create and perform music, whilst developing a lifelong enjoyment of and engagement with music.
We are fully inclusive and appropriate adaptations are made for children with additional needs so that they can access and participate in the music curriculum. Every child is given the opportunity to experience, enjoy and succeed in music, regardless of their starting point or level of musical ability.
Clarinet Lessons – A Musical Journey for Years 3&4
Over the past ten weeks, our Year 3 and 4 students have embarked on an exciting musical journey, learning to play the clarinet as part of their music curriculum. Through these lessons, they have developed essential skills that form the foundation of wind instrument playing.
Students began by mastering the correct hold, ensuring control and fluidity in their movements.
As their confidence grew, they learned to play simple melodies, following musical notation with increasing accuracy. A highlight of their learning was the opportunity to improvise within sections of a piece, allowing them to express their creativity while staying within the structure of the music.
These lessons have not only introduced our students to the joy of playing an instrument but have also deepened their understanding of rhythm, pitch, and musical expression. We are incredibly proud of their progress and look forward to seeing how they continue to develop their musical talents in the future!

About our Pre-School
Norton Little Learners provides a safe and stimulating environment for children aged 3 and 4 years old. With a real passion for Early Years, the staff share the same aim of wanting the children to learn and develop whilst having lots of fun! Through a mixture of child initiated and adult planned activities we ensure the children are well supported to develop and reach their goals. We believe that all Children are powerful learners. Every child can make progress in their learning, with the right help In Little Learners we understand the importance of working closely with and alongside the children’s parents/carers to best support their development. It is important for parents and early years settings to have a strong and respectful partnership. This sets the scene for children to thrive in their Early Years. We have themed ‘open mornings/afternoons’ where family members are welcome to come in and play. Each child has their own learning journey. This is shared with parents/carers and we welcome any input. Regular assessments are carried out within the setting and are shared with parents/carers to ensure we are all working together towards the achieve the same goals. Opportunities are provided for parents/carers to meet with their key person to discuss their child’s development.
Activities are planned based around the Early Years Foundation stage framework. Little Learners follow an ambitious and carefully sequenced curriculum, which builds learning over time. It has been designed and created alongside our Reception Teacher, with the aim to develop, enhance and promote a strong foundational knowledge of key skills and areas of learning. Our curriculum also supports children to have the best start possible, ensuring our Little Learners are ready for transition to start school at Reception age. Our aim is to deliver high quality learning through play and creativity, running a golden thread of foundational knowledge through all of our planned and child-initiated activities. Little Learners are introduced to Early Phonics sessions through learning Phase 1 phonics. This is delivered through our Phonics programme; Unlocking Letters and Sounds. We also explore and promote healthy development of children’s Personal, Social and Emotional development through the delivery of My Happy Mind sessions.
